To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the type of information overload affects electronic knowledge repository continuance.

(1) overload is not the only factor influencing EKR continuance intentions; (2) overload has a negative affect on the main success measures of the system: perceived usefulness and satisfaction; and (3) the affect of overload on the main success measure is mediated by the affect on perceived usefulness and satisfaction.
overload has no significant direct affect on continuance intention, but overload has a significant negative indirect affect on continuance through perceived usefulness and satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the type of overload affects EKR continuance.
the effect of IO on EKR usage and provides empirical evidence that IO is a key factor in determining the success of EKR.
understanding how overload affects EKR continuance, and the implications for knowledge management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type of IO affects the perceived usefulness of the system and satisfaction of the user which affects the intention of the user to continue using the EKR.
overload is not the main cause of dissatisfaction with the system, but it is a factor which can lead to dissatisfaction.
overload does not have a sufficient affect on EKS continuance intention directly but has a significant affect on two main success measures of EKS: perceived usefulness and satisfaction of EKS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the type of information overload affects EKR continuance through the mediating effects of perceived usefulness and satisfaction.
overload affects EKR continuance through its affect on perceived usefulness and satisfaction of EKR.
the overload of knowledge seekers and contributors has a negative effect on their continuance intention to use the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
overload has an indirect affect on continuance intention.
overload can be a serious problem for EKR implementation and that organizations must be aware of this and take steps to mitigate the negative affect overload has on the system.
overload is a significant issue for knowledge management initiatives and needs to be addressed.
